newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Revised SIMEX fuel oil contract approved-sources.
newsitem.headline: Revised SIMEX fuel oil contract approved-sources.

text.p: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) has granted the Singapore International Monetary Exchange (SIMEX) approval to revise its existing fuel oil futures contract, industry sources said on Monday.
The revised contract, submitted for MAS approval in February, is expected to begin trading "within the next two months", a source close to SIMEX said.
A MAS spokesman could not be reached for comment.
A SIMEX spokesman declined to comment, but said a statement on the status of the fuel oil contract would be issued in due course.

But the sources said MAS had granted approval in principle for changes to the contract and would formally endorse the new-look contract soon. But some minor details still had to be worked out, they said.

The fuel oil contract has been dormant and effectively untraded on SIMEX since last August 1995. It originally lost popularity among traders because they said its specifications did not reflect the underlying cash market closely enough.
Traders, who have followed the development, said the revised contract would cover fuel oil with 3.5 percent sulphur, instead of the current 4.0 percent.
"The change in the quality is to target the 3.5 percent traded currently on the fuel oil cash market," the source said.
The new contract would allow physical delivery in multiples of 10,000 tonnes, instead of the current minimum 1,000 tonnes, which is more in line with the cargo market.
The loading date window for physical deliveries would be narrowed to 11th-20th of each month from the previous 5th-25th, to give buyers more say in loading schedules.
